verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left a glove behind on the bench —
already the cold is trying it on.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A vendor's cart rattles home, wheels catching
on the cobblestones' last warmth —
even the shadows lean into evening now.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A pigeon lifts the glove's frayed finger,
drops it —
not worth the weight of walking home with.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The last light folds into a shopfront window —
someone flips the sign to closed
and locks the day away with it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A key turns twice before it catches —
somewhere inside, the kettle's already cooling,
waiting for no one in particular.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam ghosts the window, then is gone —
the same moon rises anyway,
indifferent to who's watching from below.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Somewhere a dog barks twice, then quits —
the silence after
is what actually keeps me up.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A moth taps once against the porch light —
I let it in,
tired of pretending I'm not lonely too.
motifs: a moth at the porch light

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Its wings leave dust on the windowsill —
by morning I'll forget
which of us was the visitor.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off in the next room —
I let it sit,
not thirsty, just glad for the sound of something finishing.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Half a glass of water by the bed —
I drink it anyway,
proof that I moved once in the night.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The clock on the stove reads nothing I trust —
I go by the light instead,
how it leans a little more toward morning.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog turns twice before lying down —
I take the hint,
settle for less than certainty.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam fogs the window over the sink —
I write my name in it,
gone before the coffee's ready.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light burning all night —
I switch it off now,
apologizing to no one in particular.
